\subsection{Re-derivation of Theorem~\ref{push:src:B.4.3}}\label{app:rederive:push-src-B.4.3}
\begin{proof}
The fundamental-group surjection in \ref{push:src:B.4.2} gives
$\pi_1(D)=1$, and hence $H^1(D;\C)=0$. We check the other
input directly. The audited root-curve direct images in E.2 and
E.3, for $\mathfrak B=\PP(3,4)$, are
\[
 \bar f_*\OO_X=\OO_{\mathfrak B},\qquad
 R^1\bar f_*\OO_X=\OO_{\mathfrak B}\oplus
                          \OO_{\mathfrak B}(-1).
\]
The coarse curve is $\PP^1$, and taking invariants by the finite
stabilizers is exact in characteristic zero. Thus
$H^1(\mathfrak B,\OO)=H^2(\mathfrak B,\OO)=0$.
Moreover $H^0(\mathfrak B,\OO)=\C$ and
$H^0(\mathfrak B,\OO(-1))=0$: in the weighted homogeneous
coordinate ring the latter would require a monomial of weighted
degree $-1$. The degree-one Leray edge sequence therefore gives
\[
 H^1(X,\OO_X)\simeq
 H^0(\mathfrak B,R^1\bar f_*\OO_X)=\C.
\]
This confirms the precise R4 input, rather than inferring
$h^1(\OO)$ from tangent-bundle cohomology. The elementary weighted
degree counts are recorded in \path{code/b_hodge_obstruction.py}.
Upper semicontinuity for the proper flat map $g$ gives
$h^1(D,\OO_D)\geq1$; flatness also follows directly from the
local equation $s=z_1\cdots z_k$.

There is a family-independent check of the required lower bound.
For any compact complex threefold $X$ diffeomorphic to $S^6$,
$c_1(X)=c_2(X)=0$ in integral cohomology, so analytic
Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch gives
$\chi(\OO_X)=\langle c_1c_2,[X]\rangle/24=0$.
The analytic index theorem used here applies without a K\"ahler
assumption; see \citet[Theorem 4.3]{AtiyahSinger1968IIIE}.
A holomorphic three-form is closed and, since $H^3(X;\C)=0$,
exact. Stokes' theorem applied to its product with its complex
conjugate, whose suitable constant multiple is pointwise
nonnegative, shows that it vanishes. Serre duality then gives
$h^3(\OO_X)=0$. It follows that
$h^1(\OO_X)=1+h^2(\OO_X)\geq1$.

For the algebraic assertion we use the precise properness
hypothesis in \citet[Section 1.D, p.120]{GrafKovacs2014Root}.
For a proper complex algebraic variety with Du Bois singularities,
the canonical map from singular cohomology to coherent cohomology
is surjective in every degree. Normal-crossings singularities are
Du Bois, including self-intersections of a global component.
Applied in degree one, this contradicts the two groups just
computed. No algebraicity of the total space is required for
this contradiction; algebraicity of the central fibre alone
would suffice.

For the simple normal-crossings assertion, suppose instead that
every nonempty intersection of irreducible components of $D$
is a $\partial\bar\partial$-manifold. This is exactly condition
(K1) in \citet[Definition 2.3]{Chen2026HodgeRoot}.
Theorem 2.4(4) of that source, which states the relevant
Steenbrink degeneration theorem under (K1), gives degeneration
at $E_1$ of the nearby Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence.
All its hypotheses have been specified: $g$ is proper,
$\mathcal Z$ is smooth, $D$ is reduced and simple normal
crossings, and its closed strata satisfy (K1). Neither a
K\"ahler metric on $\mathcal Z$ nor a local invariant-cycle
theorem is being assumed. Degeneration in total degree one
would imply
\[
 0=b_1(X_s)=h^0(X_s,\Omega^1_{X_s})+h^1(X_s,\OO_{X_s})
          \geq1,
\]
which is impossible.

Closed smooth submanifolds of a compact K\"ahler manifold are
K\"ahler. Closed strata of a Moishezon component are Moishezon:
a projective modification, followed by taking a component of
the inverse image that dominates the stratum and a general
relative linear section if needed, gives a generically finite
projective cover. Its meromorphic functions show that the
stratum has maximal algebraic dimension. Smooth Moishezon
manifolds satisfy the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma, as recalled
in \citet[Section 2.1, p.8]{Chen2026HodgeRoot}. Thus either
of the two stated conditions on components would imply (K1).
Finally, finite base change does not change the biholomorphism
type or either cohomological value of a nonzero fibre, so none
of the contradictions depends on $N$.
\end{proof}
extracts.app:rederive:push-src-C.3.5:
\subsection{Re-derivation of Proposition~\ref{push:src:C.3.5}}\label{app:rederive:push-src-C.3.5}
\begin{proof}
The raw formula without \(-h^2e/24\), its three extension checks,
and the coherent correction occur in
\cite[Proposition~7.8 and Appendix~C, Proposition~C.2]{DuEtAl2026v1}. We verify their exact use
here; the source is version~1, and version~2 omits these statements.
The global roots exist because the zero orders of \(t\) and \(t-1\)
on the simply connected uniformizing surface are divisible by three
and four. The local characters and their coprime orders give
\[
 \ell(g_1z)-\ell(z)=-\frac13,\qquad
 \ell(g_2z)-\ell(z)=\frac14,\qquad
 \ell(g_0z)-\ell(z)=\frac1{12}\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
\]
A change of logarithm adds an integral \(h\widehat\delta\) period,
so \eqref{mapsI:closing:eq:C-explicit-closing} is a well-defined torus translation.
Since \(\Pi_{c+h}=\Pi_c(I+hE)\), the two ordinary lattices agree;
the source-to-target lattice map of the identity linear part is
\(I-hE\).

For compatible logarithm lifts, covariance gives the affine defects
\[
 b_{h,c}(g_jz)-R_j(z)b_{h,c}(z)
       =\Pi_c(g_jz)\eta_j,\qquad
 \eta_1=\frac h2(\widehat u-\widehat w-\widehat\delta),\quad
 \eta_2=\frac h2(-\widehat w+\widehat\delta).
\]
Their \(\gamma\)-coordinates vanish, so the same right sides use
\(\Pi_{c+h}\). The vectors are integral for even \(h\). At the
cusp the defect is zero: \((A_0-I)\widehat\gamma=-\widehat\delta\)
cancels the increment of \(\ell\). These equations prove ordinary
and cusp descent with the stated orientation of the peripheral
loops.

For the finite comparison put \(w_j=(2\pi i)^{-1}\log s_j\).
The functions \(F/(s_1G)\) and \(Fs_2/G\) are invariant
holomorphic units on the respective full root discs. Choose
holomorphic logarithms \(\kappa_j\) of them. Then
\[
 \ell=\epsilon_jw_j+\kappa_j\pmod{\mathbb Z},\qquad
 \epsilon_1=1,\quad\epsilon_2=-1.
\]
The exact finite-to-ordinary comparison satisfies
\(\sigma_{j,c+h}-\sigma_{j,c}=h\epsilon_jw_je\).
Consequently the required finite-chart translation is
\[
 b^{(j)}_{h,c}
 =-\frac h{12}\Pi_c\widehat\gamma
       +\left(h\kappa_j-\frac{h^2}{24}\right)e.
\]
It is holomorphic on the full root disc and satisfies
\[
 b^{(j)}_{h,c}(g_jz)-R_j(z)b^{(j)}_{h,c}(z)
       -\frac{h\epsilon_j}{m_j}e
 =\Pi_c(g_jz)\eta_j.
\]
This is precisely equivariance for the source and target affine
finite actions, including the changed period column. The exact
identity
\(\sigma_{j,c+h}+b^{(j)}_{h,c}
=\sigma_{j,c}+b_{h,c}\) proves overlap agreement. Thus no real
interpolation of a multivalued period has been used.

At the cusp let \(q=e^{2\pi i s}\) and
\(C_{c,21}=\beta^{\rm part}+c+s\), which is holomorphic at
\(q=0\). The function
\[
 \widehat H=e^{2\pi i s/12}F/G
 \quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
 \widehat H^{12}=q\frac{t^4}{(t-1)^3}.
\]
The right side is a unit because \(t\) has a simple pole at the
cusp. The character formula makes \(\widehat H\) single-valued;
it therefore extends as a nonvanishing holomorphic function. Write
\(\ell=-s/12+\kappa_0(q)\), with \(\kappa_0\) holomorphic.
Since
\(\Pi_c\widehat\gamma=(6\mu,-s+C_{c,21})^t\),
the logarithmic terms cancel in \eqref{mapsI:closing:eq:C-explicit-closing}:
\[
 \bar b_{h,c}(q)=
 \left(-\frac h2\mu(q),\,
 -\frac h{12}C_{c,21}(q)+h\kappa_0(q)-\frac{h^2}{24}\right)^t.
\]
Exponentiating gives a holomorphic unit in \((\mathbb C^*)^2\).
On every toric chart its action multiplies a character coordinate
by an integral character of this unit, so it and its inverse
extend across every double curve and both triple points. The
source and target cusp lattice multipliers differ by
\((1,e^{2\pi i h\lambda_1})=(1,1)\), for
\(\lambda\in\mathbb Z^2\). They are therefore identical. The
unit multiplication commutes with their toric shears and descends.
Exponentiation of the displayed formula gives exactly the ordinary
translation on the punctured cusp. We have now verified all
three comparisons and their inverses.

The uncorrected translations have composition defect
\(-hk e/12\). The constants in
\eqref{mapsI:closing:eq:C-explicit-closing} cancel it, since
\((h+k)^2-h^2-k^2=2hk\). Hence
\[
 \widetilde F_{k,c+h}\widetilde F_{h,c}
       =\widetilde F_{h+k,c},\qquad
 \widetilde F_{0,c}=\mathrm{id}.
\]
Any difference from the fixed even-shift choice of Proposition~\ref{fam:src:A.3.1} is a scalar automorphism,
which lies in its connected $\mathbb C^*$ by Proposition~\ref{fam:src:B.4.1}. The choice therefore
has the same smooth monodromy class.

For \(h=12\), remove the actual period
\(-\Pi_c\widehat\gamma\) from \eqref{mapsI:closing:eq:C-explicit-closing}.
The remaining translation is \((12\ell-6)e\). Its exponential
is \((F/G)^{12}=K(t)\), proving
\eqref{mapsI:closing:eq:C-twelve-scalar}. The finite corrections divide it by
\(s_1^{12}\) and multiply it by \(s_2^{12}\). The original
uniformizers are retained: these are units because
\(t/s_1^3\) and \((t-1)/s_2^4\) are units. They need not be
replaced by one.

Put \(H(q)=qK(t(q))=e^{24\pi i\kappa_0(q)}\). The cusp unit
for \(h=12\) is exactly
\[
 U_{12,c}(q)=
 \left(e^{-12\pi i\mu(q)},\,
       e^{-2\pi i C_{c,21}(q)}H(q)\right).
\]
The \(\widehat\gamma\) deck transformation has multiplier
\[
 \left(e^{12\pi i\mu(q)},\,
       e^{2\pi i C_{c,21}(q)}q^{-1}\right),
\]
because \(B_0(1,0)^t=(0,-1)^t\). Multiplying these two
expressions gives \((1,q^{-1}H)=(1,K)\). This proves the
claimed comparison, including its sign, on the entire cusp
quotient. In particular the scalar representative's pole is not
an obstruction to the holomorphic map itself: its unit
representative already extends.

Finally \(w=e^{-\pi i c}\) makes six positive loops the path
\(c(r)=c_0-12r\); its endpoint is closed by the positive shift
\(h=12\). A quotient isotopy proving an order bound would still
have to patch the ordinary scalar description with the two-coordinate
cusp unit description. Scaling their additive logarithms separately
produces on their overlap a fractional
\(\widehat\gamma\)-period, which is not an integral period during
the interpolation. The separate scalings do not supply a patched isotopy. The
exact substitutions, coherent correction, finite defects, and
cusp comparison are checked in
\path{code/maps_audit/PUSH/code/d_push_monodromy.py} and
\path{code/maps_audit/PUSH/code/d_push_closing.py}, run with \texttt{python3} followed by the indicated path; these are symbolic checks of the
identities proved above.
\end{proof}
extracts.app:rederive:push-src-E.3.1:
\subsection{Re-derivation of Proposition~\ref{push:src:E.3.1}}\label{app:rederive:push-src-E.3.1}
\begin{proof}
Take the atlas consisting of the smooth base complement and the
two complete root discs.  The pullback over the $j$th root disc
is the actual torus family before its free affine quotient:
\[
 [J'_j/\mu_{m_j}]
 \mathbin{\times_{[\Delta_{s_j}/\mu_{m_j}]}}
 \Delta_{s_j}=J'_j.
\]
The atlas map, unlike $s_j\mapsto s_j^{m_j}$ on coarse spaces,
is etale.  Properness, smoothness at these roots, and the
flat equation $q=z_0z_1z_2$ at the remaining cusp were checked
in \ref{push:src:E.2.1}.  The atlas source is smooth; all its fibres are local
complete intersections of pure dimension two.  It is therefore
a proper flat Gorenstein family of complex spaces over a reduced
smooth curve.  Torus cohomology and the explicit cusp resolution
give the constant dimensions $(1,2,1)$ on every chart, including
its centre.

Apply B\u anic\u a and St\u an\u a\c sil\u a
\cite[Chapter III, Theorem 4.12(ii), pp.~134--135]{BS76}:
properness, base flatness of the coherent sheaf, a reduced base,
and constant fibre cohomology give cohomological flatness and
local freeness.  Their Theorem 4.10, pp.~132--133, supplies the
canonical analytic base-change comparison.  On the double atlas
overlap both pullbacks are identified with the direct image of
the same pulled-back family.  These comparisons commute with a
third pullback by their construction, so they satisfy the
groupoid cocycle condition.  The resulting descended vector
bundle is $R^q\bar f_*\mathcal O_X$, and its geometric fibre
comparison is the displayed one.  No assertion about the
cohomology of the reduced multiple surface is substituted for
the torus geometric fibre of the stack map.

Let $p:Y\to U$ denote any of these atlas families.  Proper analytic
duality is the canonical trace identity in
Ramis--Ruget--Verdier \cite[introduction, equation (1),
Section 1, pp.~264--265, and Proposition 2.1, p.~266]{RRV71}.
The cited article does not number its main identity as a theorem;
these are its actual locations.  The smooth-space dualizing
complex is $K_Y[3]$, and the relative Gorenstein dualizing
complex is $\omega_{Y/U}[2]$; the relevant absolute statements
are Ramis--Ruget \cite[Section 3, Theorem 1, p.~81;
Proposition 2 and the complete-intersection calculation, p.~91]{RR70}.
Cancelling $p^*K_U[1]$ in proper duality gives
\[
 Rp_*\omega_{Y/U}[2]
 \simeq R\mathcal Hom_U(Rp_*\mathcal O_Y,\mathcal O_U).
\]
The direct images just obtained are locally free, so the positive
sheaf Ext terms in the hyper-Ext spectral sequence vanish.
Degree $-2$ is therefore
$p_*\omega_{Y/U}\simeq(R^2p_*\mathcal O_Y)^\vee$.
The trace is local and invariant under the local biholomorphisms
on the atlas overlaps.  The two pullbacks of this isomorphism
thus agree with the trace for the same pulled-back family and
satisfy the same cocycle condition.  This proves descent.

For the original multiplicities $(3,4)$, \ref{push:src:E.2.1} specializes to
$\mathcal E=\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal O(-1)$,
$\omega_{X/\mathfrak B}=\bar f^*\mathcal O(1)$ and
$R^2\bar f_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O(-1)$.
The nondegenerate cusp cup product identifies
$\det R^1\bar f_*\mathcal O_X$ with this last line, and the
nonzero $[\gamma]$-subline and $H^1(\mathcal O(1))=0$ give
$R^1=\mathcal O\oplus\mathcal O(-1)$.
This derives exactly the direct images in Theorem~\ref{fam:src:A.5.2}.
\end{proof}
